# Subdued Rains for Mumbai: August to End With Below Normal Rainfall By: **AVM GP Sharma** | Edited By: **Arti Kumari**

Aug 19, 2026, 12:43 PM WhatsApp icon

thumbnail image

Key Takeaways:

* Santacruz has recorded only 286 mm of rainfall between August 1 and 19, against the August monthly normal of 560.9 mm.
* Mumbai has not witnessed any three-digit 24-hour rainfall event so far this August, and such an event remains unlikely.
* The offshore Konkan trough is inactive, while Arabian Sea westerlies are not strong enough to trigger a fresh monsoon surge.
* Light rain with isolated moderate spells is likely, but the overall intensity and spread of rainfall will remain subdued.
* Forecast Validity: Valid through the remaining days of August 2026.

##### Advertisement

##### Advertisement

Mumbai has witnessed very poor rainfall during the last one week. Santacruz recorded just 9 mm of rainfall in the past 24 hours. The observatory has accumulated just 100 mm of rainfall during the last seven days, between 13th and 19th August 2026. The total for this month so far, between 1st and 19th August 2026, is a mere 286 mm. There has been no occurrence of three-digit rainfall in 24 hours as of now, and such an occurrence is not likely either. Normal monthly rainfall for August stands at 560.9 mm. No heavy rainfall is anticipated during the remainder of this month for Mumbai and the suburbs.

[[Check your local weather forecast here]](https://www.skymetweather.com/)

Last year, Mumbai had witnessed a deluge on more than one occasion in the month of August. The city had received over 200 mm of rainfall in 24 hours on three days. The month of August itself had recorded nearly double the normal rainfall.
The good thing is that July this year was one of the rainiest months. The city had recorded 1485 mm of rainfall against the monthly normal of 919.9 mm. Together, July and August have crossed the average rainfall by a big margin. However, the remaining days of August will observe subdued activity, and typical Mumbai monsoon rainfall is unlikely.

The main triggers for the active monsoon over Mumbai are the offshore north-south trough along the Konkan Coast and a Monsoon Low/Depression forming over the Bay of Bengal. The trough is completely inactive and, at best, can give light showers. The westerly stream from the Arabian Sea is also not strong enough to stimulate heavy rainfall. Of late, the Bay of Bengal systems have been following a varied track. Against the normal route through the central parts, across Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, these systems have a tendency to move across Jharkhand and East Uttar Pradesh and go along the foothills of Nepal. This track does not favour heavy rainfall along the Western Ghats, including Konkan.
Presently, there is a monsoon depression positioned over North Jharkhand and adjoining Southwest Bihar. It is likely to move west-northwest and get placed over North Chhattisgarh and Southeast Uttar Pradesh. It is expected to weaken into a low-pressure area over that region. The weakening of the system will fail to initiate any fresh monsoon surge from the Arabian Sea. Light rainfall, with isolated moderate rainfall patches, is likely during this week and even beyond. Overall, the intensity and spread of rainfall will remain poor and, therefore, will be unable to catch up with the normal rainfall for the month.

FAQ

## **Is heavy rainfall expected in Mumbai during the remaining days of August 2026?**

No significant heavy rainfall is anticipated. Light rain with isolated moderate spells may occur, but widespread or typical heavy Mumbai monsoon rainfall is unlikely.

## **How much rainfall has Mumbai's Santacruz observatory received in August so far?**

Santacruz has accumulated 286 mm of rainfall between August 1 and 19, 2026, against the monthly August normal of 560.9 mm.

## **Why has rainfall activity weakened over Mumbai?**

The offshore north-south trough along the Konkan Coast is inactive, Arabian Sea westerlies are relatively weak, and recent Bay of Bengal systems have been taking a more northerly track that does not favour strong rainfall over Konkan and Mumbai.

The following is the monthly breakdown of the weather in Mumbai.

### January

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: January") ]

January is the coolest month of the year for Mumbai, with the mean daily minimum being 16.4 °C and the mean daily maximum being 30.1 °C. [[ 11 ]]() [[ 12 ]]() The nightly lows may vary between 13 °C and 20 °C. Chilly northern winds during the day make the city seem cooler than it is. Generally, clear skies, with some [smog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smog "Smog") – especially in the early morning – are the norm. The days are dry, and the nights relatively [humid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid "Humid") . January is also associated with the [deciduous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deciduous "Deciduous") trees in the city shedding their leaves.

...

title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: March") ]

The month of March sees a mean minimum temp of 20.6 °C and a mean maximum temp of 32.7 °C. [[ 11 ]]() During the transition from dry to humid weather in mid-March, the temperature might hit 38 to 40 °C. This high, however, is due to hot dry winds from [Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat "Gujarat") . By mid-March the temperatures may hit 37 °C, with the lows at 24 °C. Humidity is unbearable, and smog affects the city. New leaves sprout from deciduous trees. The all-time high day temperature for March was recorded in 2018 at 41.7 °C. [[ 14 ]]()

### April

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: April") ]

The temperatures and humidity are still high. However, the cooling effect of the sea breezes makes its presence felt. The high temperature stays around 35.1 °C and daily lows are around 23.2 °C. Plants are in full bloom in April.
### May

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: May") ]

May is the hottest month of the year for Mumbai with the cool sea breezes providing some relief. The daily maximum hovers around 34.5 °C and the daily low is 29.1 °C. [[ 11 ]]()

### June

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: June") ]

June marks the beginning of the [monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon "Monsoon") period in [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai") . The beginning of the month is characterized by a continuation of the summer with increased [humidity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humidity "Humidity") . The official date for the monsoon to hit the city is 10 June. [[ 15 ]]() This period is marked by [thunderstorms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thunderstorms "Thunderstorms") and often windy conditions as the monsoon establishes itself over the city.
Rainfall activity intensifies as the month goes on, leading into the wettest month, July. The max and min mean daily temperatures are measured at 34.5 °C/26.6 °C. [[ 11 ]]()

### July

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: July") ]

[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mumbai_monsoon.jpg) Waterlogging due to showers

In this month the city receives the maximum amount of [rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rain "Rain") . July and August are characterized by almost non-stop rain and weeks of no sunshine. A continuous [monsoon current](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon_current?action=edit&redlink=1 "Monsoon current (page does not exist)") covers the entire [western coast of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_coast_of_India?action=edit&redlink=1 "Western coast of India (page does not exist)") during this period.
Rainfall activity is less stormy and more constant with a relatively constant breeze from the West or South West. It is not uncommon for parts of the city to be waterlogged during periods of persistent heavy rain. This affects the city's public transport system often leading to long delays. During periods of severe [precipitation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precipitation "Precipitation") , the city's commuter rail system is often suspended because of water logging and poor visibility.

The average maximum temperature for the month is around 29.8 °C with the average minimum at 25.5 °C. [[ 11 ]]() Average monthly rainfall is 919.9 mm in Santacruz and 768.5 mm in Colaba. [[ 1 ]](:2-1) The highest 24-hour rainfall in the history of Mumbai was recorded at the Santacruz observatory of the [India Meteorological Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_Meteorological_Department "India Meteorological Department") on 26 July 2005. On this day, a [record 944 mm rainfall](https://en.
wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharashtra_floods_of_2005 "Maharashtra floods of 2005") fell over the city, causing large-scale flooding, claiming several lives and causing large-scale [property damage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Property_damage "Property damage") . [[ 16 ]]()

### August

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: August") ]

The weather in August is almost identical to July. Towards the latter half of the month, rainfall activity tends to lessen. The coolest days of the monsoon season are often in August. The max temperature might drop to 29.3 °C during the day and 24.5 °C at night. [[ 11 ]]()

### September

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Climate_of_Mumbai&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: September") ]

In September the intensity of rainfall decreases. The monsoons officially end in the 3rd week of September. September has unsettled weather.
